equity_bridge.item: Remaining Fuel for Growth one-off restructuring cash (2027), after tax
equity_bridge.note: Analysis.json / H1 2026 guidance: ~GBP 1.0bn cumulative one-off cash restructuring and transformation cost to reach fixed costs below 19% of revenue by end-2027, c. GBP 350m in 2026. With ~GBP 700m spent 2024-2026 (FY2025 restructuring/other project costs 195m; H1 2026 cash on adjusting items 133m), ~GBP 300m remains for 2027, GBP 220m after 27% tax. The flows are built from ADJUSTED EBITDA, which excludes these costs, so they are charged here, undiscounted (slightly conservative). The 2026 portion is treated as netted against the H2 2026 free cash flow that is also outside the June net-debt vintage.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management medium-term guidance (Core Reckitt +4-5% LFL, ~83% of the continuing base; MJN low-single-digit, ~17%), blended and haircut ~0.5pt for the Russia Hygiene exit and FX translation drag; equity CAGR rejected as the base because it is negative purely from capital returns and impairments
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-3.2% 5yr) diverges from revenue (+0.3%) and EPS (+23% 5yr, inflated by the GBP 1,245m Essential Home disposal gain in FY2025 and the FY2021 loss year). Book value has shrunk because GBP 1.2-1.4bn/yr dividends plus GBP 0.2-1.3bn/yr buybacks exceed retained earnings and because of GBP 0.8-1.0bn impairments in FY2020, FY2023 and FY2024. None of the historical CAGRs is a usable forward growth anchor: FY2020 was the COVID Lysol/Dettol peak (reported FCF 3,032m, owner FCF 2,940m) and the FY2025 end point still includes Essential Home.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - finance income): FY2020 2,940; FY2021 1,156; FY2022 1,746; FY2023 1,875; FY2024 2,051; FY2025 1,530. The owner series falls faster than reported (5yr -12.3% vs -11.1%) because SBC rose from GBP 15m to 101m while FCF fell, but at 0.7% of revenue SBC is immaterial to the valuation; the FY2025 dip reflects the capex step-up to 4.3% (615m) and GBP 200m+ of restructuring cash under Fuel for Growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Reckitt as a 3-4% grower with a slowly rising high-20s EBITDA margin: Core Reckitt at the low end of its 4-5% medium-term LFL guidance, MJN flat-to-low-single-digit, Fuel for Growth absorbing the Essential Home stranded costs, capex easing from the FY2025 investment peak, cash returned through a progressive dividend and rolling buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: Top-of-range execution: Emerging Markets and innovation (Activ Botany, Mucinex 12HR, Durex Intensity) carry 5% growth for three years, Europe recovers, margin expands 2.5pp, NEC litigation closes without material cost after the Inman defence verdict, and the 2.5-year portfolio clean-up earns a re-rating.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural volume weakness in Europe and North America, MJN decline, China VMS disruption and an NEC settlement in the low billions of pounds compress growth to 1-2% and the margin back toward the H1 2026 trough; the market pays a 15x FCF exit multiple for a de-rated staple.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Reckitt on the continuing Core Reckitt + MJN perimeter only, from an FY2026E revenue base built on H1 actuals and the reiterated FY2026 outlook, with SBC expensed, leases as debt, NCI and the non-operating Essential Home consideration (vendor loan note, 30% Vestacy stake) handled once in the bridge, and all discounting in GBP at a single 7% WACC. Reported history is a different perimeter and is shown for audit, not extrapolated. The three scenarios differ on volume growth, the margin trajectory versus the H1 2026 trough, and whether NEC litigation costs cash; risk is carried in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: NEC (necrotizing enterocolitis) product-liability litigation against Mead Johnson in US federal MDL and state courts: no outstanding verdicts after the Aug 2026 Inman defence win, but hundreds of cases remain; a settlement in the low billions is the bear case
Europe (33% of Core) has been in LFL decline since 2025 on Auto Dish promotional intensity and value-seeking consumers; the base case needs the guided H2 2026 return to growth to hold
FY2026 margin guidance (24.9-25.6% Core+MJN AOP) requires an H2 well above the 23.6% H1 print; stranded costs from Essential Home and oil-linked input inflation are only partly mitigated
MJN (17%) is explicitly non-core and may be sold; a disposal at a low multiple or a resumed structural decline removes a fifth of the cash flow base
Net debt rose to 2.5x EBITDA after the GBP 1.6bn special dividend and GBP 3bn of H1 returns; a USD 2.5bn bond is now current and refinancing cost drives the guided GBP 320-340m finance expense
Terminal value is capped at 18x FCF in base; the valuation is ~60% terminal and moves ~10% per 1pt of WACC

Vestacy transitional-services revenue (GBP 235m in H1 2026) is excluded from the base and valued at zero; the FY2026 reported group revenue will therefore print ~GBP 13.1bn against the 12.7bn used here

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E continuing revenue = Core Reckitt + Mead Johnson Nutrition only. Built as H1 2026 actual GBP 6,176m (Core 5,110 + MJN 1,066, +1.8% reported, +2.6% LFL) plus H2 2026E ~6,525m (H2 2025 Core+MJN 6,286m x ~1.04: Core LFL guided to accelerate to reach FY +4-5%, MJN low-single-digit, ~1pt FX drag). Excludes (i) Essential Home (GBP 1,852m in FY2025; sold to Advent 31 Dec 2025, so the FY2025 group figure of 14,205 is NOT the base) and (ii) Vestacy transitional-services revenue (GBP 235m in H1 2026 at a GBP 12m AOP, winding down as separation completes; valued at zero). Russia Hygiene (held for sale, ~1-2% of Core, completing H2 2026) is still inside the base; its exit is absorbed in the year-1 growth rate.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 June 2026, post the 25-for-24 consolidation of Feb 2026: ~634.2m ordinary shares net of 38,950,759 treasury shares (H1 2026 note 9: 671.6m pre-consolidation in issue less 26.86m consolidation reduction = 644.75m, less 12.04m bought back in H1, plus 1.58m treasury released; ties to the H1 weighted average of 646.4m basic) plus 1.8m dilutive awards (H1 2026 adjusted-EPS footnote: 646.4m basic / 648.2m diluted). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The GBP 500m buyback announced July 2026 is value-neutral under this convention and its post-June cash is not in the June net debt either, so count and debt are the same vintage.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company-defined net debt at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 interim, net debt reconciliation): cash 878 + 119 in held-for-sale, short-term borrowings 2,695 (incl. USD 2.5bn bond now current, GBP 723m CP, 73 lease), long-term borrowings 7,468 (incl. 223 lease), net of derivatives. Includes lease liabilities of GBP 296m (treatment A). Up GBP 2,822m from Dec 2025 because the GBP 1,578m special dividend, GBP 826m FY25 final dividend and GBP 599m buyback were paid in H1. The H2 2026 free cash flow (seasonally the stronger half; ~GBP 1.0-1.1bn) is roughly offset by the interim dividend (~GBP 560m) and buyback run-rate, so carrying the June figure against a FY2026E base understates equity by well under 1% per share.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments' add-back GBP 101m (RKT.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:8399; 2024: 85). No separate equity-award tax withholding line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 across the kpis history); awards are satisfied from treasury shares.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF anchor on the FY2025 reported (CSV) basis: OCF 2,297 - capex 615 = 1,682, less SBC 101, less finance income 51 = 1,530. This is the whole group including Essential Home and is a LEVERED figure (after GBP 344m interest paid), so it is an audit anchor only; the projections are unlevered component builds from the continuing-ops revenue base and the terminal value is bridged to equity through net debt. Interest income is stripped from the anchor because the matching assets (vendor loan note, equity instruments, Vestacy stake) go into the equity bridge at carrying value instead; Reckitt is a net-debt company so the stripped amount is small.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases GBP 879m (FY2024: 1,328m; H1 2026: 599m, completing the GBP 1bn programme). A further 'up to GBP 500m' programme was announced July 2026. Reckitt is a genuine repurchaser, so the flat count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.fx_note: Same currency, different denomination: statements and all flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quote GBp/share; it is a fixed denomination bridge, not a market rate, and does not go stale. Parity: no second listing; the implied market cap (636.0m shares x current_price / 100) is ~GBP 32-33bn, which ties to the GBP 31.6bn stockanalysis.com figure in info.json taken at the lower 22-Sep-2026 price.
inputs.price_note: Yahoo Finance chart API regular-session close for Friday 9 Oct 2026 (the closing-auction print after the 15:30Z continuous close); 52-week range 3,664-6,523p. Not an after-hours print.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the currency of the flows: 10y gilt ~4.5% risk-free, 5.0% UK/global ERP, consumer-staples beta ~0.65 gives a cost of equity ~7.75%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (bond fair value 8.1bn vs book, 2026 refinancing at EUR/USD coupons), 3.4% after 27% tax; weights ~78% equity (market cap ~GBP 32-33bn) / 22% debt (net debt 9.4bn) give 6.8%, rounded to 7.0%. The same 7.0% is used in all three scenarios: NEC litigation, European volume weakness and MJN deterioration are charged in the bear flows and the bear weight, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: A: leases as debt. Lease liabilities (GBP 296m at 30 June 2026: 73 current + 223 non-current) are inside the company's net debt figure used in the bridge; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows. Ongoing lease-asset renewal (new lease liabilities ran GBP 56m in H1 2026, ~GBP 100m/yr, ~0.5-0.8% of revenue) is charged through the capex path, which is set ~0.5pp above management's 'around 4%' capex guidance. D&A at 3.1% includes right-of-use depreciation, which is added back and then re-charged via that capex uplift, so the lease is charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are GBP 35m of equity and GBP 2m of H1 profit (immaterial); deducted once in the equity bridge, flows left at 100%.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, 10-year explicit horizon (owner-FCF margin is still moving through year 5 as Fuel for Growth savings and category mix lift the Core+MJN margin and capex normalises from the FY2025 4.3% peak). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: a large-cap consumer health/hygiene/nutrition operating company is the owner-FCF row; the non-US adaptations file was applied for GBP-denominated WACC, the GBP/GBp denomination bridge, the single lease treatment, NCI and the matching-asset rule (vendor loan note, Vestacy stake and equity instruments added to the bridge because their income sits below operating profit and never enters the flows). EBITDA margin paths are PRE-SBC (company adjusted EBITDA of GBP 3,979m on FY2025 is after the GBP 101m SBC charge; the engine deducts sbc_pct separately, so the path is AOP margin + ~3.1pp D&A + 0.7pp SBC). H1 2026 EBITDA is deliberately blank in core_metrics (the cash-flow D&A line of 391 is contaminated by the GBP 125m Russia held-for-sale remeasurement); the margin anchor is the FY2026 Core+MJN AOP guidance of 24.9-25.6% (H1 actual 23.6%, H2 guided 'much stronger'). The FY2025 reported revenue/FCF/EPS history is a different perimeter from the forward build (Essential Home inside), so historical CAGRs are reported but not used for growth selection. Pension: GBP 286m surplus vs GBP 220m obligations, net +66m, left out of the bridge. Russia Hygiene disposal group: assets 149 = liabilities 149 after the GBP 125m write-down to expected net proceeds, so zero in the bridge. Fuel for Growth one-off cash remaining after 2026 (~GBP 300m pre-tax) is charged as a bridge deduction because adjusted EBITDA excludes it; from 2028 the programme is complete and the margin path carries its benefit.

bear.narrative: Volume-led stagnation plus a litigation bill. Europe stays in decline under Auto Dish promotional pressure and value-seeking consumers, the US consumer stays 'tough' and seasonal OTC under-delivers, Emerging Markets slow as China VMS and Russia drop out, and MJN resumes its structural decline: 1-2% growth. The pre-SBC EBITDA margin falls to 26.5% (AOP ~22.7%, near the H1 2026 run-rate of 23.6%) as stranded costs are not fully mitigated, input-cost inflation is only partly priced and the NEC multi-district litigation produces adverse state-court verdicts and a settlement; the 1.5-3.3pp margin gap to base over the first five years is ~GBP 1.3bn pre-tax, the order of magnitude of a plausible settlement plus defence costs. Capex stuck at 4.5%, cash tax 28%, growth consumes working capital. Terminal growth 2.0% and a 15x cap, the multiple a de-rated staples name gets.

base.narrative: Core Reckitt delivers the lower half of its 4-5% LFL range, MJN grows low-single-digit, FX and the Russia exit cost ~0.5pt: 3.5% blended for four years fading to 2.5% terminal. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 29.0% in FY2027 (AOP ~25.2%, the midpoint of FY2026 guidance, plus 3.1pp D&A and 0.7pp SBC) lifts 1pp over five years as Fuel for Growth offsets stranded costs and mix improves, then holds. Capex 4.5% including lease renewal, easing to 4.2%. Cash tax 27% per the FY2026 guided adjusted ETR (24.7% in FY2025 was flattered by uncertain-tax-position releases). Working capital neutral: the -6% NWC position would release cash on growth, but Fuel for Growth is unwinding payables and the H1 2026 outflow was GBP 377m. Terminal: 2.5% growth, capped at 18x FCF.

bull.narrative: Core Reckitt sustains the top of its range: Emerging Markets keep compounding high-single-digit on Dettol Activ Botany, Durex and India/China, Europe returns to growth in H2 2026 and holds it, Mucinex 12HR Cold & Fever and Lysol adjacencies keep North America positive, and MJN stabilises as US WIC share and China recover. Margin expands 2.5pp to a 31.5% pre-SBC EBITDA (AOP ~27.7%) as Fuel for Growth over-delivers and premiumisation mix compounds; capex normalises to 4.0%; negative NWC releases 5% of each year's revenue increase. NEC litigation resolves on the back of the Inman defence verdict with no material cash cost. Terminal growth 3.0%, still capped at 18x.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the NEC product-liability MDL is a genuine tail (an adverse bellwether outcome or a large state-court verdict would force a settlement; the 31 Aug 2026 Inman defence verdict lowers but does not remove it), European volumes have been negative for 18 months, and H1 2026 margin (23.6%) sits well below the full-year guidance range. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things at once: Europe back to growth, a 2.5pp margin expansion, and a clean litigation exit. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
